A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TetraJet-v2. All 16 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original OLMo-2 pretraining, downstream evaluations, ablations, oscillation measurements and precision-switching experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity tests, Muon experiments, memory measurements and GPU efficiency results.

M1.justification: The double-block quantization, backward RHT, weight-resetting and OutControl procedures are retained. v2 adds an optional OsciReset variant that tracks a sensitivity-selected subset, typically 5% of weights, instead of every weight (Section 3.2; Appendix C, Algorithm 3). The OutControl calibration description provides implementation detail rather than establishing a changed selection method.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpus, language-model evaluation datasets and downstream task suite are retained. Muon experiments and larger Llama2-structured timing models extend optimizer, model and execution configurations without adding a documented dataset, language, domain or learning task.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained Quartet and NVIDIA accuracy baselines, v2 Table 12 evaluates Wang et al. (2025), Tseng et al. (2025), and FourOverSix. The first two were previously cited but not evaluated. TransformerEngine-FP8 becomes an evaluated efficiency comparator in Section 5.3 and Appendix G.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Muon experiments and extensive latency/throughput protocols across matrix dimensions, model sizes, batch sizes, sequence lengths and GPUs. It also revises the reported 150M/370M learning rate from 4e-4 to 3e-4 and Hadamard block size from 32 to 16. These revisions do not establish reruns. The headline 52B/107B/212B token counts already appeared in v1 Appendix A.

E4.justification: New analyses test OsciReset tracking subsets, oscillation thresholds and suppression starting times; examine overlap between oscillation and quantization error; assess Muon compatibility; and isolate finer weight-scaling overhead (Appendices C, D.2, F and G.1). Earlier block-scaling, rounding, OutControl, loss-decomposition and precision-switching analyses remain, often relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging training perplexity over the final 50 steps is retained. New descriptive percentages and parameter sweeps do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical scores, but v2 adds substantial baseline, Muon, sensitivity, memory and efficiency results. Examples include 35.03 validation PPL with 5% tracking versus 34.95 with full tracking (Table 7), and a 1.67× Transformer-block speedup over TE-FP8 in the specified RTX5090 benchmark (Figure 5). The existing activation-only ΔPPL is corrected from +0.43 to +0.44.

T1.justification: v1 Section 5.1 includes an inconsistent Hadamard equality with an extra 1/sqrt(2) multiplying the Kronecker product of already normalized matrices. v2 Section 4.1 removes that equality and retains the correctly normalized block recursion. The gradient-unbiasedness reasoning remains; no new convergence theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The three principal techniques and 51.3% performance-gap reduction claim remain. v2 adds measured 1.67× speedup over FP8 as a headline contribution, whereas v1 explicitly lacked hardware efficiency evaluation. It also claims a currently optimal fully-FP4/RHT configuration and identifies oscillation as the dominant failure mode.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting unsuccessful transfer from vision models to supervision density and training duration, and distinguishes high quantization error from dynamic oscillation (Section 6.1; Appendix C.3). It adds optimizer-compatibility interpretations and replaces the hardware-unavailability limitation with architecture/scale limits and an explicit qualification that full-model speedups cover forward/backward computation rather than complete training-system overhead.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project-code link, OutControl calibration details such as accumulating activation norms for approximately 50 steps near 1% training progress, subset-tracking pseudocode and state/sharding information. It also documents CUDA kernels, CUDA 12.8, GPU models, FlashAttention-2, TransformerEngine RMSNorm and timing configurations. Code availability is stated in the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Metis and FourOverSix to related work, along with optimization and implementation references. It more explicitly positions oscillation mitigation as complementary to representational-accuracy approaches. The established relationship to TetraJet, vision-model oscillation methods and outlier-control work remains; moving Related Works to Appendix A is structural.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves to Appendix A, tracking/training pseudocode to Appendix C, and detailed ablations to Appendix D. The abstract and introduction are revised, and the former combined conclusion/limitations section becomes separate discussion, conclusion and limitation subsections. An impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v1 Figures 1–2 merge into v2 Figure 1, existing analyses move into appendices, and new comparison, sensitivity, memory and timing tables accompany throughput and latency plots. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly could not test its central efficiency promise on NVFP4 hardware. v2 addresses that important gap with measured GPU results, including full-model forward/backward comparisons, and strengthens validation through additional baselines, robustness checks and implementation details. These are substantial gains despite unchanged headline accuracy scores. Accuracy evidence remains limited to small OLMo-2 models, complete training-system speedups remain unmeasured, and the new optimality language exceeds the demonstrated scope.
